content.title: Nvidia in China, Paramount's WBD bid, Campbell's: 3 Things
content.description:
The Trump administration has reportedly given Nvidia (NVDA) the green light to sell its H200 chips to China.

Paramount Skydance (PSKY) has launched a $108 billion hostile takeover bid for Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), a counter to Netflix's (NFLX) $72 billion offer that the studio accepted last week.

Lastly, the Campbell's Company (CPB) reported fiscal first quarter earnings results.

content.title: Stocks to Watch Tuesday Recap: Nvidia, AutoZone, PepsiCo, Campbell’s
content.summary: 🔎 Nvidia (NVDA): President Trump said he would let Nvidia export its H200 chip to China, and the U.S. would receive a 25% cut. He said the government would take a similar approach to AMD (AMD) and Intel (INTC) exports.

content.title: Campbell’s Stock Fell on Continued Sales Decline. It’s Making a Bigger Bet on Rao’s.
content.summary: Campbell’s has been battling slowing sales and fallout from tariffs. It is buying almost half of Rao’s Italy-based producer.

content.title: Tariffs Dent Campbell’s Soup Sales
content.summary: Campbell’s logged lower profit and revenue in its latest quarter as weak demand for snacks continued. It also said it has agreed to acquire a 49% interest in La Regina, the maker of Rao’s pasta sauce.

content.title: Campbell's Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Net Sales Drop 3% Y/Y
content.summary: CPB beats EPS estimates even as sales and margins slip, with cost pressures and a planned La Regina stake shaping its 2026 outlook.

content.title: Campbell’s to pay $286M for 49% stake in Rao’s pasta sauce supplier
content.summary: The transaction will better position the CPG giant to continue growing the recently acquired brand by ensuring quality and accelerating innovation.

content.title: Campbell (CPB) Q1 Earnings: Taking a Look at Key Metrics Versus Estimates
